gap: No result ChatGPT got states a lab-measured bass limit for any of its picks: Erin's Audio Corner measured the Edifier M60 (ChatGPT's $199.99 'premium' pick) on a Klippel Near-Field Scanner (review dated 2026-01-26), and its bass is 3 dB down at about 67-70 Hz and 6 dB down at 62.3 Hz. GadgetGuy measured the Logitech Z407's subwoofer system peaking at 64 Hz, so the Z407 is strong right where the M60 drops off.
standout_why: I read stackandvalue.com (cited, dated 2026-10-24) in full. It gives only maker power ratings (Pebble Pro 10/30 W RMS, Z407 40 W RMS, R1280DBs 42 W RMS) and Bluetooth versions. It has no measured figures and no latency. The rival dupple.com says in its own title that it ranks by stated specs. I could not open the other cited pages: TechRadar, Tom's Guide and Tom's Hardware returned only a title to WebFetch, and Bash fetches needed approval I didn't have. PC Gamer (top-results, uncited) also returned only its headline. None of the search snippets for those pages showed Klippel or spinorama data for the M60, but I can't rule out that one of them prints a measured figure. That is why the score is 2 and not 3.
decides: It confirms the split ChatGPT made, and gives it numbers. The M60 is a clean, small 2.0 pair (Erin's Audio Corner frequency deviation 2.8 dB over 300 Hz-5 kHz), but its bass is 6 dB down at 62.3 Hz. Spinorama rates it 4.6 as it is and 7.33 with an ideal subwoofer, so a shopper who wants bass for games or movies gets more from a 2.1 set like the Z407. A shopper who wants music and voice on a small desk without a sub is fine with the M60. None of this decides the PC-specific question of Bluetooth lag: no named lab measured latency on any candidate.
